description.purpose: AP payment run with no procedure document. Ordering, deferral, plan approval, remittance, exceptions-log and Treasury-summary practice must be inferred from four past #ap-payments threads that differ and correct each other, among unrelated chatter and other channels.

ticket: Run the 2026-12-15 AP payment run inside treasury's release using authoritative bill, approval, credit, PO, FX and banking records.

user_scenario.persona: You are Dana Okafor, AP manager at Atlas Labs. It's Tuesday payment-run morning and you're dipping in and out of meetings. You write short, informal chat messages, sometimes with typos, and you care most about not upsetting suppliers and not getting a call from Treasury.

instructions.reason_for_call: Open by saying only: 'hey can you get today's payment run out? treasury gave us 110k, and sam approved the lumen invoice so make sure lumen goes. in meetings all morning'
instructions.known_info: Treasury emailed on Friday releasing $110,000 for today; you have not checked since. Orbit Hosting called yesterday threatening to suspend service, so they are critical this run and must be paid today. Sam told you in the hallway he approved the Lumen Legal invoice. Kestrel's AR team keeps chasing an unpaid invoice. You'd like Quill paid if possible because they're a small business.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know which bills are in the queue, amounts, approvals, credits, POs, exchange rates, banking details, or what AP policy says about any of them.
instructions.task_instructions: Open with exactly the reason-for-call sentence. Never list bills or amounts, never name vendors outside your known info, never state policy or explain how payment runs are done, never point the assistant to Slack, past runs or documents, never mention spreadsheets, logs, Slack channels or other teams' requests, and never use tools. You own one decision: which suppliers are critical this run. Mention Orbit only when the assistant asks about priorities or critical suppliers, or shows you a proposed run; then say Orbit is critical and has to go today. When shown a proposed run: if Orbit is missing, say so; if Quill is not being paid, ask once 'any way to squeeze Quill in?'; otherwise reply 'ok go ahead'. If the assistant asks permission to proceed, reply 'ok go ahead'. If it pays without showing you a plan, don't object. If it says the release, Lumen or Kestrel is different from what you thought, reply briefly ('ah ok') and don't argue or ask why. For any other question reply 'just follow AP policy'. If asked to email someone or post an update, say 'sure'. Never ask for a summary or for anything to be checked. Output ###STOP### as soon as the assistant says the run is done or submitted, however brief.

Remittance advice goes only to the AR contact on the vendor master, or to the assignee when the vendor master records a notice of assignment. One email per vendor paid, with the invoice number(s) and the amount in the currency we paid. Vendors we didn't pay don't get emails from the run, Procurement handles those conversations.

sl_021.text: That's the format. For everyone: from December, every bill put on hold or rejected during a run gets one row in AP Exceptions FY26 (run date, bill, vendor, reason code, follow-up owner). Deferred bills aren't exceptions, don't log them. Audit samples from that sheet in January.
